title: Daily activity and visual discrimination reflects the eye organization of weaver ant Oecophylla smaragdina (Insecta: Hymenoptera: Formicidae)
why: Oecophylla smaragdina: sweep-26 opened this preprint and records that it gives the interommatidial angle of the weaver ant's compound eye in its Figure 4E only (its text gives 710 to 790 facets and lens diameters of 13 to 18 µm), so a reader of the figure could log interommatidial_deg for the species. Ogawa et al. 2023 (10.1007/s00359-023-01629-7), which main read in full (oa-5), states no interommatidial angle in its text. Returned by the harvest queries "Oecophylla vision", "Oecophylla eye" and "Oecophylla visual acuity" and by both web searches for visual acuity; not opened in this unit.

Rusa unicolor: an open-access Folia Morphologica article ranked first (journals.viamedica.pl) and second (as https://dx.doi.org/10.5603/fm.a2021.0015) for the web search "sambar deer pupil shape"; the results showed no title. A morphology journal ranking first for the sambar's pupil suggests an anatomical study of the sambar eye, which would describe the pupil and may describe the tapetum. Pupil shape and the tapetum carry within a genus (rule 3). Not opened.

why: Rusa: a study of the reflecting structure of the tapetum across taxonomically diverse vertebrates; it came back third for the web search "Rusa tapetum lucidum", and its species list was not visible, so it may include a sambar or rusa deer. Not opened; title and address from the search result.

title: Retinal cone topography of artiodactyl mammals: influence of body height and habitat
why: Rusa acuity_cpd: a survey of retinal cone topography across artiodactyls; main's wanted lines sweep-91 and sweep-10 say the 2024 Cervidae review cites it for the cone streak of the moose and for the northern pudu lacking that streak. As a topography study it mapped retinas of its own sample, so its species list is not a compilation of published values, and it may include a sambar or rusa deer, whose cone densities could give an anatomical acuity. The acuity searches returned the Cervidae review at four addresses, a white-tailed deer visual-discrimination paper, a roe deer blue-light study, a USDA deer item, the Wildlife Online deer overview, a Brazilian veterinary article and PubMed Central and DTIC pages whose titles were not shown, forum and photograph pages, the Javan rusa Wikipedia page and patents; none gives a Rusa acuity. Main holds 222 rows over 96 taxa from Veilleux and Kirk 2014 (in hand), none a Rusa. Neither the harvest listing nor this unit's searches returned the paper; main's wanted line sweep-91 gives its DOI and authors, so this line leaves the DOI, authors and year empty, since this unit takes them only from the harvest output or a search result. Not opened.
get: journal via library (the same work as main's wanted line sweep-91)

why: Chalcophaps: the harvest returned it for "Chalcophaps vision"; it relates eye morphology to ocular optics across amniotes, and the stored abstract names no species, so its eye-dimension data may include an emerald dove, from which an anatomical acuity and a receptor spacing could follow. The same paper is on the wanted lines of harvest-29 and harvest-38 for unrelated genera, so the match may come from its title words and the genus may be absent from its text. Authors are left blank because neither the harvest listing nor a search result shows them. Not opened.

why: Chalcophaps eye_movement: a video study of blinking in 591 bird species, mostly in zoos. The harvest returned it for "Chalcophaps visual acuity", so its text probably names an emerald dove, and its abstract says that nictitating-membrane blinks occur mainly on head movement, so it may say whether the emerald dove bobs its head while walking. Authors are left blank because neither the harvest listing nor a search result shows them. Not opened.

Miltochrista miniata: a University of Ljubljana repository record ranked first for the web search "rosy footman spectral sensitivity"; the result showed no title, so the record may be a thesis or paper on photoreceptor spectral sensitivity that includes the rosy footman. The other results of that search were a mayfly spectral paper, a PubMed Central page whose title was not shown, a topic page and rosy footman photograph pages. Not opened.

title: Visual abilities in two raptors with different ecology
why: Parabuteo unicinctus: the stored abstract says the authors measured visual acuity, foveal characteristics and visual fields in Harris's hawks and black kites. Main read it only from its abstract (birds rows), and Potier et al. 2018 (10.1242/jeb.177295, read in full on main, oa-3) logs only the width of the blind area above the head (75.5 degrees) for this species and attributes its raw data to this paper, so the full text should give the horizontal visual field (fov_h_deg), and its foveal measurements may give a receptor spacing (interreceptor_deg). It is the top result of all four web searches for the genus and is already on main's wanted lists (birds, sweep-7, harvest-32). Authors are left blank because neither the harvest listing nor a search result shows them. Not opened.

why: Parabuteo interreceptor_deg: a single-author review of eye anatomy and foraging vision in predatory and scavenging diurnal raptors, returned by the harvest for "Parabuteo visual acuity"; Harris's hawk is one of the predatory raptors whose eyes and foveae have been measured, so its text or tables may give a photoreceptor or ganglion-cell spacing for the species. Already on main's wanted lists (harvest-32, harvest-37). Not opened.

title: Morphological traits of the eyes of Lepidoptera indicate selection for binocular vision in both diurnal butterflies and nocturnal moths
why: Choristoneura and Miltochrista, acuity_cpd and interommatidial_deg: an eye-morphology study of 2,730 specimens of 224 butterfly and moth species sampled across tribes, as main's wanted lines describe it. Its species table (Table S2) has not been read on main (oa-12 holds 10 rows over 6 taxa from the text), and its specimens were measured for the study, so a tortricid such as a Choristoneura or a lithosiine tiger moth such as Miltochrista miniata may be among the species, with eye measurements from which an anatomical acuity or interommatidial angle could follow. The acuity searches for both genera returned no eye measurement: for Choristoneura, Wikipedia pages on two Choristoneura species, Plazi and Zenodo taxonomic records, defoliation and aerial-survey pages, budworm reports and a Michigan State thesis file whose title was not shown, and acuity papers on other animals; for Miltochrista, human acuity and health pages. Neither this unit's harvest listings nor its searches returned the preprint; main's wanted lines harvest-30, harvest-32, harvest-33, harvest-34, harvest-38 and harvest-40 hold it with its Research Square DOI, so this line leaves the DOI, authors and year empty, since this unit takes them only from the harvest output or a search result. Not opened.
